title: the DSG Deepearth areas 14-15

banner.title: THE DSG DEEPEARTH AREAS 14-15, R540: printed pp. 86-88 (pdf 87-89) - the individual area key crosses the reclaimed lakebed and the great water: Area 14 Reclaimed Caverns (the former subterranean lake almost completely filled with water, drained only by the diligent pech miners' blocked waterways - the two north inflows and south outflow continuations; the Area 5 river made dangerous by its 500-foot waterfall into a deep pool, then running placid beneath about six feet of airspace; the eastern river diving underground at the base of a mountain waterfall plunging several thousand feet through a sinkhole, rapid all the way to Area 14 but keeping a 10-foot minimum airspace and a navigable sinkhole access; the three long narrow parallel caves east-west, each opening onto the river and united by connecting passages; the heroic walls-of-stone dikes holding the water out while small streams still flow; the pech bridge over the eastern river at the middle cavern's end, joining the partially excavated 8-by-12-foot descending cavern of many miles; the water-polished uniformly smooth floors, walls and ceilings devoid of formations; the well-organized 300-miner community at the middle cavern's center with its iron and copper deposits; the monster roster - scrags, shambling mounds, a gibbering mouther, cave crickets, throat leeches, ropers, an owl bear, rust monsters and cockatrices; the Area 15 kuo-toan sabotage war - dikes damaged, rivers diverted, 20-to-25-strong war parties every few months, always defeated but never ceasing; the fanatically guarded copper and iron ore stockpiles; and the engineering marvels - the drains and centrifugal pump powered by the bridge-side giant water wheel, the lever-shifted ventilation over the coal-burning smelting plant and forge venting through a one-foot aperture to a remote mountain valley, and the stone town with its buildings stacked three or four deep and its ore wagons blocking the avenues), and Area 15 the Upper Lake of Deepearth (the almost completely water-filled chamber on its rock walls and columns, the level a dozen or more feet short of the ceiling, boat-traversable over most of its extent; the west shoreline shelf - 10 to 400 feet wide, the only dry land, reached through the partly carved dry tunnel from Area 6 with its intelligent-built stone piers and the 50% chance of 1d6 moored longboats; the cold still waters 10 to 100 feet deep, marred only where the twin Area 14 rivers enter; the center drain hole matching its outflow to the inflow, regulated by the kuo-toa and their boulder works; the great kuo-toan numbers and the blind fish of the inky depths; the domes over food-raising, quarters, hatcheries, government and recreation with their breathable air pockets where escape is virtually impossible; the giant catfish, pike, gar, lamprey, trout, perch and salmon, the water nagas, giant otters, giant crabs, giant snapping turtles, scrags and lacedons; the aboleth - perhaps the most purely evil denizens in all Deepearth, avoiding the kuo-toa but seizing all others as slaves; the aquatic fungi and brown algae with no minerals known; and the domed city by the drain - six hexagonal major domes, 150 feet across and 50 high with 20 feet of air, their corridors and rooms nested around the swim-through elevator holes)
banner.provenance: the DSG scan (archive.org item advanced-dungeons-dragons-1st-edition), pdf = printed + 1; the text read from the IA djvu OCR (djvu.txt lines ~11005-11253) with the pdf Acrobat-Capture layer as the second read (idx 396-400 = the printed pp. 86-89 windows, with idx396's stream emitting the p. 87 area 14 body in its first block before the p. 86 tail blocks - a page-block order anomaly, all text present); the compiled-tables appendix has no reprint of this prose. A CLEAN-READ ROUND: both machine reads agree on every load-bearing number - the 500-ft waterfall, the six-foot and ten-foot airspaces, the three caves, the 8x12-ft bridge cavern, the 300 miners, the 20-to-25 war parties, the one-foot vent, the three-or-four-deep stacking, the 50% longboat chance, the 10/400-ft shelf, the 10/100-ft depths, and the six 150/50-ft domes with 20 ft of air; the garbles settled cross-read (the djvu '5096' for the capture's 50%, the capture 'ld6' for the djvu's 1d6). SEAMS: the R518 water travel (the river routes and the navigable sinkhole), the Monster Manual denizens (the pech, kuo-toa, aboleth, kraken-less lake fauna and the monster roster), the PHB wall of stone, the R521-R522 mining (the iron and copper works), and the R503 re-grain. A ZERO-FLIP ROUND: the pp. 75-98 Deepearth child remains open until the setting lands in full (the R527/R533-R539 precedent - the gap report is NOT in the git add). Nothing auto-credits.
banner.sentinel: A procedural-plus-prose round: no tables pin. The numbers pin as consts per the R508 convention - the waterfall and airspace feet, the cave and dome counts, the bridge cavern's 8x12, the 300 miners, the war-party bounds, the vent aperture and stacking depths, the longboat chance and dice, the shelf and depth bounds, and the dome dimensions with their air cap, with the 1d6 dice pinned as a count-and-sides pair. The geography, denizens, resources and unique-features prose pins as bools for both areas. The water-travel/MM/PHB/mining/R503 seams are noted; the Deepearth child stays open; nothing auto-credits.

consts.name: dnaiFallsFt
consts.comment: the course of the river flowing from Area 5 is made dangerous by a 500-foot waterfall that plunges into a deep pool before resuming a more placid journey downstream through Area 14.

consts.name: dnaiAirspaceWestFt
consts.comment: the latter part of the Area 5 river's journey runs through a cavern that allows about six feet of airspace over the surface of the river.

consts.name: dnaiAirspaceEastFt
consts.comment: the easternmost river, rapid from its first moments underground, here has airspace over the water of a minimum of 10 feet high.

consts.name: dnaiCaveCount
consts.comment: the area itself comprises three long, narrow caves running parallel along an east-west access, each opening onto the river and united by numerous connecting passages.

consts.name: dnaiBridgeCavernHtFt
consts.comment: the bridge over the easternmost river connects with a partially excavated, partially natural cavern that descends slowly over many miles; this cavern is eight feet high.

consts.name: dnaiBridgeCavernWidFt
consts.comment: the descending bridge cavern is 12 feet wide.

consts.name: dnaiPechCount
consts.comment: the pech have created a well-organized community in the center of the middle cavern; a total of about 300 of these industrious miners live here.

consts.name: dnaiKuoPartyLow
consts.comment: the kuo-toan war parties from Area 15 generally number about 20-25 individuals (the low bound).

consts.name: dnaiKuoPartyHigh
consts.comment: the kuo-toan war parties generally number 20-25 individuals (the high bound), attacking any creatures they run into but especially seeking out the pech.

consts.name: dnaiVentApertureFt
consts.comment: when the pech smelting plant operates, the pumping system pulls the smoke through a vent to be released on the surface, eventually exiting through a one-foot-wide aperture into a remote mountain valley.

consts.name: dnaiStackLow
consts.comment: the pech community's stone buildings tend to be stacked three or four deep (the low bound).

consts.name: dnaiStackHigh
consts.comment: the stone buildings are stacked three or four deep, with narrow winding alleys providing access (the high bound).

consts.name: dnaiLongboatPct
consts.comment: there is a 50% chance that 1d6 longboats are moored at the stone piers of the west shoreline at any time.

consts.name: dnaiLongboatDice
consts.comment: the moored longboats number 1d6 (the die count).

consts.name: dnaiLongboatSides
consts.comment: the moored longboats number 1d6 (the die sides).

consts.name: dnaiShelfLowFt
consts.comment: the dry-land shoreline shelf of rock ranges from 10 to 400 feet wide (the low bound) - the only part of the entire chamber where one can walk on dry land.

consts.name: dnaiShelfHighFt
consts.comment: the shoreline shelf ranges from 10 to 400 feet wide (the high bound).

consts.name: dnaiDepthLowFt
consts.comment: the lake's depth varies from 10 to 100 feet (the low bound).

consts.name: dnaiDepthHighFt
consts.comment: the lake's depth varies from 10 to 100 feet (the high bound).

consts.name: dnaiDomeCount
consts.comment: the domed city of the kuo-toa is organized in a pattern of six major domes laid out in a hexagonal pattern.

consts.name: dnaiDomeDiaFt
consts.comment: each of the six major domes of the kuo-toan city is about 150 feet in diameter.

consts.name: dnaiDomeHtFt
consts.comment: each of the major domes is about 50 feet high.

consts.name: dnaiDomeAirFt
consts.comment: the top 20 feet of each major dome is filled with air, with an elaborate network of corridors and rooms nesting around elevator shafts - holes connecting the water-filled levels, up and down which the residents simply swim.

bools.name: dnaiLakeReclaimed
bools.comment: these caverns were once part of a subterranean lake and were almost completely filled with water; only the diligent efforts of a group of pech miners blocked off the water flow and enabled air to fill the bulk of this area - accessible only through the two waterways flowing in on the north side and the continuations of these streams flowing out from the south.

bools.name: dnaiEastRiverRoute
bools.comment: the easternmost river goes underground at the base of a huge mountain waterfall, plunging several thousand feet from an isolated gorge to disappear through a sinkhole and begin a hidden course; since the sinkhole allows fairly easy access to the water below, this river provides a navigable means of reaching Area 14.

bools.name: dnaiPechDikes
bools.comment: by dint of heroic applications of walls of stone the pech have built dikes to keep the water out of the three caverns; small streams still flow through but menace no one, and the area provides both dry and river routes deeper into the earth.

bools.name: dnaiSmoothCaves
bools.comment: because these caves were filled with water until relatively recently (geologically speaking) they are devoid of common cave formations - floors, walls and ceilings almost uniformly smooth, polished by the action of water through many centuries.

bools.name: dnaiPechMining
bools.comment: with their unerring instinct for potential mining sites the pech opened the caverns to mining and have profited - major deposits of iron and copper have been discovered here, with mining parties journeying from the central community and returning with loads of ore; all sorts of fungi now thrive in the remote corners.

bools.name: dnaiMonsterRoster
bools.comment: an assortment of monsters roams these caverns, living off the fungi and any prey they can catch: a small group of marine trolls (scrags), several shambling mounds, a gibbering mouther, many cave crickets, throat leeches, ropers, an owl bear, rust monsters, and cockatrices.

bools.name: dnaiKuoRaids
bools.comment: the area is subject to the depredations of the Area 15 kuo-toa, who would like to see the entire area filled with water again - they regularly attempt to sabotage the pech efforts by damaging the dikes or diverting the river to flood the caverns; the men-fish have always been defeated in these conflicts but send up another war party every few months, forcing the pech to constantly maintain their guard.

bools.name: dnaiPechHoard
bools.comment: the rivers flowing into the region have enough airspace to maintain a constant supply of fresh air; the pech operate a number of large-scale mining operations and have stockpiled large amounts of copper and iron ore which, beyond limited amounts for tools and weapons, they seem to have little use for - nonetheless they guard their hoard with fanatical dedication.

bools.name: dnaiPumpingPlant
bools.comment: the pech have built an elaborate pumping system relying on drains in the low spots of each of the three main caverns and a huge centrifugal pump diverting water to Area 15 - powered by a giant water wheel where the bridge crosses the eastern river, spinning a large fan in a drainage pipe that can move an incredible amount of water when the rivers run high.

bools.name: dnaiSmeltingForge
bools.comment: simply by shifting a large lever the pump can activate a ventilation system over the pech smelting plant and forge, located in the center of their small stone community - it can burn great quantities of coal in a few hours, its smoke pulled through a vent to exit into a remote mountain valley.

bools.name: dnaiStoneTown
bools.comment: the pech community is well-organized and neat - stone buildings, large stone wagons used for pulling loads of ore, several parked about the community at all times, often blocking one or more important avenues.

bools.name: dnaiLakeChamber
bools.comment: this subterranean chamber is almost completely water-filled; walls and columns of rock support the ceiling over mostly open water, the level falling a dozen or more feet short of the ceiling in most places though some ceiling drops to or below water level - boat travel is possible over most of the Upper Lake.

bools.name: dnaiWestShoreline
bools.comment: at the west end lies a shoreline reached through a dry tunnel branching down from Area 6 - partly natural caverns, much of it carved by intelligent denizens, serving as one of the major avenues to the surface world, with stone piers obviously built by intelligent creatures.

bools.name: dnaiLakeDrain
bools.comment: the lake's waters are cold and mostly still, marred by turbulence only where the twin rivers from Area 14 enter; in the depths near the center a small hole drains water to the lower levels of Deepearth, its outflow almost perfectly matching the inflow so the level remains fairly constant.

bools.name: dnaiKuoDomestead
bools.comment: the kuo-toa dwell here in great numbers along with many varieties of blind fish in the inky waters; they have built a number of great domes over food-raising, living quarters, fingerling hatcheries, government centers and recreation - mostly water-filled but each holding a small pocket of breathable air at the top, where air-breathing prisoners are left since escape is virtually impossible.

bools.name: dnaiLakeFauna
bools.comment: giant catfish, giant pike, giant gar, lamprey and numerous trout, perch and salmon lurk in the depths, along with water nagas, giant otters, giant crabs, giant snapping turtles, scrags and lacedons (marine ghouls).

bools.name: dnaiAboleth
bools.comment: aboleth may also be encountered in the depths of the lake - perhaps the most purely evil denizens in all of Deepearth; found in small groups, they actively avoid the kuo-toa, but all other creatures are fair game: given the chance they seize any unfortunate characters who cross their path, dragging them far into Deepearth as slaves.

bools.name: dnaiLakeResources
bools.comment: water is obviously plentiful and the existing air quite breathable; a number of varieties of aquatic fungi and brown algae are commonly found in the water, and no minerals or other resources are known.

bools.name: dnaiDrainRegulation
bools.comment: the drain at the bottom of the lake is regulated by the kuo-toa so it always drains away water at the proper rate - the men-fish have placed boulders around the drain to block off part of the hole if the inflow slows, and other rocks can be pulled out of the way to accelerate the flow.

bools.name: dnaiDomeCity
bools.comment: the domed city of the kuo-toa lies next to the drain in one of the deepest parts of the lake - typical of kuo-toa communities, with its six hexagonal major domes and the elevator-shaft holes the residents simply swim up or down.

examples.note: the river routes: the 500-ft waterfall, the six-foot western airspace, the ten-foot eastern minimum.

examples.expr: m['dnaiCaveCount']() != 3 or m['dnaiBridgeCavernHtFt']() != 8 or m['dnaiBridgeCavernWidFt']() != 12 or m['dnaiPechCount']() != 300
examples.note: the reclaimed caverns: three parallel caves, the 8x12-ft bridge cavern, the 300 pech miners.

examples.expr: m['dnaiKuoPartyLow']() != 20 or m['dnaiKuoPartyHigh']() != 25 or m['dnaiVentApertureFt']() != 1 or m['dnaiStackLow']() != 3 or m['dnaiStackHigh']() != 4
examples.note: the raids and the works: the 20-25-strong war parties, the one-foot vent aperture, the buildings stacked three or four deep.
the shoreline moorings: the 50% chance of 1d6 longboats.

examples.expr: m['dnaiShelfLowFt']() != 10 or m['dnaiShelfHighFt']() != 400 or m['dnaiDepthLowFt']() != 10 or m['dnaiDepthHighFt']() != 100
examples.note: the lake measures: the 10-to-400-ft shelf, the 10-to-100-ft depths.

examples.expr: m['dnaiDomeCount']() != 6 or m['dnaiDomeDiaFt']() != 150 or m['dnaiDomeHtFt']() != 50 or m['dnaiDomeAirFt']() != 20
examples.note: the kuo-toan city: six hexagonal domes, 150 feet across, 50 feet high, 20 feet of air.
